judged_text: updateEvent's fallback was changed to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares each calendar's externalId against the very externalCalendarId that is absent in that branch, so the fallback always evaluates to undefined. Updating a booking whose calendar reference carries no externalCalendarId now calls events.update with calendarId undefined and fails, leaving the existing calendar event with stale times after reschedule.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback for `selectedCalendar` was changed to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it ends up comparing each `cal.externalId` to `undefined`/`null`, which will almost always return no match and thus `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. The diff does not show any subsequent defaulting to "primary" for `updateEvent` (unlike `createEvent`, which explicitly uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`), so this can result in calling the Google API with an undefined `calendarId` when updating bookings whose calendar reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (a case visible in `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent` where `calenderExternalId` is set to `null` if absent).
